chunks: Dangers of lithium batteries and prevention. The question: What are the dangers of Lithium-based battery chemistries? How can these be prevented?
The main danger of a lithium battery is thermal runaway. A cell stores a lot of energy in a sealed package and has a flammable liquid inside.
If it is overcharged, crushed, shorted or overheated, it can heat itself until it vents flammable gas and catches fire.
Safety is built in layers so that no single failure leads to that.
Think of the squeal when a microphone is held near its own speaker.
A little sound goes in, the speaker makes it louder, the microphone picks up the louder sound, and it snowballs. Thermal runaway is a heat version.
Heat speeds up chemical reactions that make more heat, and above roughly 100 to 150 degrees Celsius the loop sustains itself.
Unlike the squeal, you cannot simply move the microphone away.
Every stage releases heat and hands the cell a higher temperature, so the dashed arrows are the feedback that makes runaway self-sustaining.
Prevention means stopping the chain at the trigger, or limiting how fast heat escapes and spreads.
Thermal runaway: self-feeding heating that ends in venting and possibly fire.
Electrolyte: the flammable liquid or gel inside the cell that carries lithium ions ("LiPo cell materials"). Separator: the thin film that keeps the electrodes apart.
If it fails, there is an internal short. Venting: the cell releasing hot gas through a weak point to relieve pressure.
Protection circuit (BMS): electronics that cut the connection on overvoltage, overcurrent or heat ("Battery management system features").
A 2 Ah cell at 3. 7 volts holds 2 times 3. 7 equals 7. 4 watt hours, which is about 26. 6 kJ of energy. Normally that energy comes out slowly through the device.
If the cell is crushed, the energy can come out in seconds as heat inside the cell.
The defenses are layered: the charger limits voltage, a protection chip cuts the cell off, a fuse blows, and the case protects it from impact. That is the whole idea.
"The main danger is thermal runaway.

Lithium cells have a flammable electrolyte and a lot of stored energy, and abuse like overcharge, overdischarge, shorting, puncture or heat makes them self-heat until they vent and burn, sometimes with toxic gas.

You prevent it in layers: cell-level separator and vent, a protection IC with voltage, current and temperature cutoffs plus a fuse, a proper CC/CV charger with a temperature check, mechanical protection, a safer chemistry like LiFePO4, and good handling."
